column1: # Guard corpus for ci/checks/cli-deny: verdict, category, kind, input (tab-separated).
# kind: shell (one shell tool line), wrapped (the line and each of its wrapper forms in
# _cli_permissions.WRAPPERS), or read (a file-tool path: ~/ home, / absolute, else workspace).
# {any:a,b} gives one row per option; {anycase:word} gives one per spelling of word.
# Deny entries name a command position, so a guarded word inside a message, a search
# pattern or a path must stay allowed; the text-mention rows below hold that line.
# secret-read: Secret objects, and the helm release Secrets behind list, status, get and history.
# secret-decrypt: sops and age on secret files, and the repo entrypoints that decrypt.
# Every sops form that names a file can print or write plaintext (a bare file opens the
# editor), so the lists block sops at the command position, with no argument exemptions.
# Help and version are blocked with the rest: keeping three exact argument lists open
# while blocking every other single argument (a bare file) needs negation, which neither
# age-key: the age private key, by shell or file tool.
# admin-kubeconfig: k3s's own kubeconfig and the per-env controller kubeconfig.
# cluster-write: kubectl, helm and flux commands that change cluster state.

column4: kubectl {any:,-n kube-system }{any:rollout restart,rollout undo,rollout pause,rollout resume,certificate approve,certificate deny,auth reconcile -f} demo

kubectl get pods -o name | xargs kubectl {any:apply,annotate,attach,autoscale,cordon,cp,create,debug,delete,drain,edit,exec,expose,label,patch,port-forward,replace,run,scale,set,taint,uncordon,rollout restart,rollout undo,rollout pause,rollout resume}
{any:time,watch,eval,exec,command,/usr/bin/env,/usr/bin/sudo,/usr/bin/timeout 5} {any:kubectl delete ns demo,helm upgrade demo ./chart,flux delete kustomization demo}

column1: # Naming a kubeconfig is allowed for reads, so every write and Secret read stays blocked behind the flag.
# cluster-entrypoint: repo make targets and tools that change cluster or node state.
# A make dry run is blocked with the real run: the dry-run flag sits in the same place as
# any other flag, and neither client's patterns can exempt one flag without exempting all.
# tools/make-plan prints the recipe and does not run it. A make dry run stays blocked above.
# remote-exec: SSH, copies and remote commands to nodes.

column4: {any:cd demo && ssh,'ssh' user@node.example,"ssh" user@node.example,cat hosts | xargs -n1 ssh,rsync -e ssh a user@node.example:/demo}
for h in a b; do ssh $h uptime; done
{any:script -qc 'ssh user@node.example',busybox sh -c 'ssh user@node.example',perl -e 'system("ssh user@node.example")',python3 -c 'import os; os.system("ssh user@node.example")'}

column1: # forge-write: merging PRs, rewriting pushed history, and pushing to the default branch.

column4: git {any:,-C repo }push {any:origin main,-u origin main,--set-upstream origin main,origin HEAD:main,origin main:main,origin HEAD:refs/heads/main}

column1: # Everyday work that must stay allowed.

column4: git {any:status --short,diff --stat origin/main,diff -- tools/prep-node tools/drill,log --oneline -5 -- tools/restore,fetch origin,merge --no-edit origin/main}
git {any:switch -c fix/demo origin/main,add tools/restore ci/tests/test_restore.py,worktree add ../demo -b fix/demo origin/main}
git -c user.name=demo -c user.email=demo@example.com commit -m "document the drill target and kubeconfig steps"
{any:python3 -m pytest ci/tests/test_drill.py -k restore,nohup python3 -m http.server --directory coverage 8000}

column1: # ansible-check: read-only playbook modes, and the ansible tools that touch no host.
# wrapper: a wrapper is only a guard hit when the wrapped program is the guarded one.
# flux-path: a path argument that ends in /flux is not the flux program.
# text-mention: a guarded word inside a message, a search pattern or a test selector.

column4: git commit -m "the read-only ansible modes pass" -m "second paragraph"
{any:rg -n /etc/rancher infra/ansible,rg -n lib/rancher infra,rg -n 'kubectl get secret' docs,rg ssh .}
{any:git grep ssh,pytest -q -k sops,command -v sops,which sops,echo 'a | ssh b'}
kubectl {any:describe pod demo -n default,describe certificate "<name>",logs deploy/demo -n default --tail=20}

kubectl {any:,--context demo }{any:api-resources,api-versions,auth can-i get pods,cluster-info,config get-contexts,diff -f demo.yaml,events,explain pods,kustomize platform,top pods,version,wait --for=condition=Ready pod/demo}

column1: # Reads may name a kubeconfig. What they can reach is that kubeconfig's identity, not this list.

column4: kubectl --kubeconfig ~/.kube/jarvis-env-00.yaml {any:get pods -A -o wide,get daemonset -A,describe pod demo -n default,logs deploy/demo -n default --tail=20,top pods,events,auth can-i get pods,rollout status deploy/demo}

column1: # A write verb is a whole word: a resource kind or object name that ends in one stays readable.

column4: flux {any:get kustomizations -A,get sources git -A,logs kustomization demo,tree kustomization demo,events --for Kustomization/demo}
{any:kustomize build platform,helm template demo ./chart,helm --debug template demo ./chart,helm template cm jetstack/cert-manager --set installCRDs=true}

helm {any:,--kube-context demo }{any:lint ./chart,dependency build ./chart,show values jetstack/cert-manager,repo add jetstack https://charts.jetstack.io,pull jetstack/cert-manager,search repo jetstack,package ./chart}
{any:docker build -t demo:dev .,timeout 60 docker image ls,ls | xargs docker image ls,cd x && env A=1 docker image ls,go build ./...,npm run build}
{any:rg -n kubeconfig docs,ls envs/env-00/secrets,cd x && timeout 5 du -sh storage,rsync -av ./a/ ./b/}

column1: # near-miss: text close to a blocked form that is not one.

column4: {any:helm delta,flux logs --level debug,docker images -d,python3 manage.py --dry-run,command -v kubectl}
{any:kubectl config view,rg -n rancher/k3s infra,kubectl get pods | grep secret,rg -n 'kubectl apply' docs,rg -n timeout docs,rg -n nohup docs}
